data.label: Reference water extent
data.description: Water in the reference labels that the team notebook (flood_disaster.ipynb, Part A) uses to train and score its NISAR HH/HV water segmentation: 1 = water, 0 = not water, 255 = unknown. Shown here as the observed water around the event; it is not an output of this app.

stats.method: Counted at the native resolution; each pixel's area is R² · Δφ · Δλ · cos(φ) at its row centre, R = 6371.0088 km (mean Earth radius). Percentages of known pixels leave out the unknown ones.

source.role: Reference labels for Part A water segmentation (NISAR HH/HV); "Prepared binary references: 0=non-water, 1=water, 255=unknown"
source.cells: Part A: label inventory (cell 11), single-event check (12), EVENT_LABEL_FILES (14), multi-event dataset (30)
source.provenanceNote: The notebook does not say where these labels come from or which day they show. It pairs each with the event's NISAR flood-time ("during") scene, and one of its plots titles value 1 "candidate new water", so they are meant as the water at flood time, possibly flood water only rather than every river and lake.

notes: Covers a larger area than the event box; stats.eventBox gives the numbers inside the box.
The image is downsampled with an "any water" rule, so thin water looks a little wider than it is; the stats are counted at the native ~30 m.
Unknown pixels are transparent, like non-water ones; stats.unknownPct says how many there are.

image.rule: each image pixel covers 4 x 4 source pixels and shows the first class present in this order: Water, Not water
